messages:
erin: deploy-bot opened a bump v0.9.2 -> v0.9.3 for merged PR #9134 (infra: rotate secrets and add s3 lifecycle). PR touches infra/ and .github/actions. Should we keep patch bumps for infra/ci-only?

matt: i'd rather not. customer-facing semver should reflect runtime/user-visible changes. infra churn = buildmeta.

kai: agree. but we need a clear process so we don't accidentally skip patches that matter (migrations, flags). suggestion: path-based default skip + explicit [force-patch] tag.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scanned files: ["infra/secrets/rotate.yml",".github/actions/ci.yml"]. Current rule: bump-on-merge unless title has [skip-patch]. No path heuristics.

sre-oncall: ops note: if we skip bump we must still add an ops changelog entry and record the infra rev in release-tracker for audits.

erin: proposal: change deploy-bot to treat PRs that only touch roots ^(infra|deploy|docs|\.github|tools)/ as non-bump by default. Add [force-patch] to override and a PR-template checkbox "Non-customer-facing infra change (skip patch)". Also stop creating public tags until bump decision confirmed; create internal tags instead.

matt: +1. avoids force pushes and noisy public releases.

kai: i'll open two tiny PRs: one for the template checkbox and one adding an ops_changelog section to the release generator (internal only).

deploy-bot: I will open a config PR to implement path heuristics and internal tagging flow. ETA: 48h.

erin: action items assigned. holding v0.9.3 from being published. marking resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
